kept.title: Incorrect multiline detection for trailing comma enforcement
kept.explanation: The variable 'lastTokenOnNewLine' was replaced with 'nodeIsMultiLine' to check if the node spans multiple lines. The later conditional changed to use 'nodeIsMultiLine' instead of comparing the end line of the node with the penultimate token, which is a more reliable measure. However, the original code condition was 'lastTokenOnNewLine = node.loc.end.line !== penultimateToken.loc.end.line;' which checked if the last token is on a new line relative to the penultimate token, but now it was changed
kept.suggestion: Revert to checking if the last token is on a new line relative to the penultimate token rather than just node multiline status. Specifically, restore 'lastTokenOnNewLine = node.loc.end.line !== penultimateToken.loc.end.line;'. Use this lastTokenOnNewLine for conditional checks rather than nodeIsMultiLine.
kept.failureAfterChange: When the node is single-line but the comma is on a new line (or vice versa), the rule misreports incorrect missing or unexpected trailing commas, causing false positives or false negatives.

verdicts.reason: The finding points out a concrete defect that exists in the code after this change: the previous check distinguished whether the last token is on a different line than the penultimate token (which is more precise for dangling comma enforcement), whereas the new code only checks if the node is multiline overall. This can cause incorrect reports of trailing comma issues in edge cases. Thus, the finding correctly identifies a defect introduced by the change.
